claim: Acropolis adult ticket is EUR 30 year-round with a compulsory hourly timed slot (arrive within 15 min either side); the official government combination ticket was discontinued in April 2025.
quote: the official combination ticket administered by the government has been discontinued as of April 2025

claim: Greece's April 2025 ticketing reform put the Acropolis in its own EUR 30 category, abolished the seasonal winter discount and set tiered prices (EUR 20/15/10/5) for other sites by visitor volume.
quote: A. Acropolis of Athens: 30 euros · B. Archaeological sites and museums (over 200,000 visitors): 20 euros · C. ... 15 euros · D. ... 10 euros · E. ... 5 euros

claim: Post-reform individual prices in Athens: Ancient Agora EUR 20, Olympieion EUR 20, Roman Agora EUR 10, Hadrian's Library EUR 10, Kerameikos EUR 10, Aristotle's Lyceum EUR 5; Kerameikos closed for works with a July 2026 target reopening.
quote: Closed for works at time of writing, due to reopen in July 2026

claim: The Ephorate of Antiquities of Athens closed the Kerameikos archaeological site and museum from Monday 5 May 2025 'till further announcement' for infrastructure upgrade works.
quote: works to upgrade the infrastructure of the Archaeological Site in the framework of the project of the Ministry of Culture

claim: Acropolis Museum summer hours (1 Apr-31 Oct): Mon 09:00-17:00, Tue-Sun 09:00-20:00, Fri 09:00-22:00; admission EUR 20 full / EUR 10 reduced.
quote: Summer (Apr 1 - Oct 31): Mon: 9am-5pm; Tue-Sun: 9am-8pm; Fri: 9am-10pm — General admission: €20

claim: The National Archaeological Museum's single ticket rose from EUR 12 to EUR 20 on 1 January 2026, with no winter/summer distinction.
quote: the price of the single NAM ticket will be set at 20 euros from January 1, 2026, without distinction between winter and summer seasons

claim: Museum of Cycladic Art: permanent collection EUR 12 (reduced EUR 9), open Mon/Wed/Fri/Sat 10:00-17:00, Thu 10:00-20:00, Sun 11:00-17:00, closed Tuesdays.
quote: Monday, Wednesday, Friday, Saturday: 10:00-17:00 · Thursday: 10:00-20:00 · Sunday: 11:00-17:00 · Tuesday: Closed

claim: The Odeon of Herodes Atticus hosted farewell celebrations in June 2026 and then closes for a multi-year restoration.
quote: retreat into silence for a few years

claim: Greece's Central Archaeological Council approved a restoration of the Odeon of Herodes Atticus in February 2026; works start July 2026 and the monument stays closed at least three years.
quote: The maintenance, restoration, and upgrading of the Odeon will take at least three years from the start of the works, during which time the monument will remain closed.

claim: Official ministry listing for the Acropolis: EUR 30 full / EUR 15 reduced covering the Acropolis and its Slopes, summer hours 08:00-20:00 with last entrance 19:30 tapering from 1 September; closed only on 1 Jan, 25 Mar, 1 May, Easter Sunday and 25-26 Dec; as of 13 August 2026 the site elevator is out of order and the on-site toilets are shut for renovation.
quote: Tickets Full: €30, Reduced: €15 ... for the archaeological site of the Acropolis and its Slopes ... Summer: 08:00 20:00 Last entrance: 19:30 ... Urgent notification (13.08.2026): We inform you that the elevator at the Acropolis archaeological site is out of order.

claim: Ancient Agora of Athens costs EUR 20 full / EUR 10 reduced covering both site and museum, open 08:00-19:30 in summer (last entry 19:00).
quote: Tickets Full: €20, Reduced: €10 Valid for the archaeological site and the museum of the Ancient Agora of Athens ... Summer: 08:00 19:30 Last entrance: 19:00

claim: Roman Agora of Athens costs EUR 10 full / EUR 5 reduced, summer hours 08:00-20:00 (last entry 19:30).
quote: Tickets Full: €10, Reduced: €5 Valid for the archaeological site of the Roman Agora of Athens ... Summer: 08:00 20:00 Last entrance 19:30

claim: Kerameikos is listed at EUR 10 full / EUR 5 reduced for site and museum, summer 08:00-20:00.
quote: Tickets Full: €10, Reduced: €5 Valid for the archaeological site and the museum of Kerameikos.

claim: The Olympieion (Temple of Olympian Zeus) costs EUR 20 full / EUR 10 reduced, summer 08:00-20:00 (last entry 19:30).
quote: Tickets Full: €20, Reduced: €10 Valid for the Olympieio archaeological site ... Summer: 08:00 20:00 Last entrance: 19:30

claim: Hadrian's Library costs EUR 10 full / EUR 5 reduced, summer 08:00-20:00; the Ministry's free Digital Tour Guide app launched in March 2026.
quote: Tickets Full: €10, Reduced: €5 ... the Digital Tour Guide application ... will be launched and made available to the public free of charge as of March 2026.

claim: National Archaeological Museum official hours for summer 2026 (4 May-15 Nov): Wed-Mon 08:00-20:00, Tue 13:00-20:00, admission EUR 20; EU citizens up to 25 enter free with ID.
quote: Summer season from May 4th, 2026 to Νovember 15th, 2026 Wednesday – Monday: 08:00 – 20:00 / last admission 19:30 Tuesday: 13:00 – 20:00 ... Admission fee 20 €

claim: Practical Acropolis advice for 2026: booking a timed slot is mandatory, the south-east (Dionysus) entrance no longer reliably beats the main gate queue, cruise crowds land from about 10am, and there is no shade on the rock.
quote: It is now mandatory to book a time slot in advance ... Less visitors knew about this entrance ... lines are now similar

claim: In July 2025 Greece's Ministry of Culture shut the Acropolis until 17:00 for safety during a heatwave, with national work stoppages from noon to 5pm.
quote: Greece's Ministry of Culture ordered a partial closure of the 2,500-year-old Acropolis until 5pm on Tuesday "for the safety of workers and visitors, owing to high temperatures."

claim: Athens' first major 2026 heatwave peaked 18-22 July at 40-43C with the Acropolis closing roughly midday to 5pm on extreme days; alerts come via EMY and the 112 civil-protection system.
quote: The first major heatwave peaked between July 18-22, 2026, with temperatures reaching 40-43°C ... the Acropolis closed "typically from midday to 5pm" on extreme-heat days.

claim: The Acropolis cap is 20,000 visitors a day, down from 23,000, allocated in hourly slots of 3,000 (08:00-09:00) and 2,000 (09:00-10:00), trialled from 4 September 2023 and permanent from 1 April 2024.
quote: 8-9 am: 3,000 visitors; 9-10 am: 2,000 visitors ... The Acropolis will now permit a maximum of 20,000 visitors daily, down from the previous 23,000.

claim: Athens editors rate Pangrati, Koukaki, Kolonaki, Exarcheia, Kypseli, Psyrri and Mets as the neighbourhoods worth walking, each with a distinct food and cafe scene.
quote: Pangrati stands out as capturing 'Athens right now' ... Koukaki balances local charm with accessibility ... Psyrri transforms from daytime workshop district to evening social hub

claim: For a first Athens base, Plaka or Koukaki suit first-timers, Syntagma is the transport hub, Psyrri is the nightlife pick, and Omonia needs street-by-street vetting.
quote: Omonia requires careful vetting—"it really is street-by-street, and some spots feel rough late at night."

claim: The official Athens city guide places Anafiotika, the Cycladic-style quarter built by workmen from Anafi, inside Plaka alongside Agios Nikolaos Ragavas, the Lysicrates Monument and the Pikionis pathway, and warns visitors to expect crowds.
quote: Anafiotika: Founded by workmen from the island of Anafi ... be prepared for the crowds

claim: The Panathenaic Stadium is open 08:00-19:00 March-October and costs EUR 12 (EUR 6 reduced), with a 30-minute audio guide in 11 languages included.
quote: March – October: 8:00 AM – 7:00 PM ... General Admission: €12.00 ... An automatic audio guide is included with ticket purchase

claim: Private after-hours Acropolis visits cost EUR 5,000 for up to five people at 07:00 or 20:00 on Tuesdays, Fridays and Saturdays; bookings rose from 72 in 2025 to 80 confirmed by the start of the 2026 season.
quote: by the start of the summer season alone, there were already eighty confirmed bookings

claim: The hop-on hop-off bus is only worth it for mobility limits, extreme heat or the Piraeus link; central Athens sights sit within a 20-minute walk of each other and the metro costs EUR 1.20 a ride.
quote: Save the €20 and explore on foot — you'll have a richer experience ... the metro handles everything beyond walking distance for €1.20 a ride.

claim: The Benaki Museum of Greek Culture on Vasilissis Sofias charges EUR 12 (EUR 9 reduced), opens Mon/Wed/Fri/Sat 10:00-18:00, Thursday to midnight and Sunday to 16:00, and is closed Tuesdays.
quote: Monday, Wednesday, Friday & Saturday: 10 am - 6 pm; Thursday: 10 am - midnight; Sunday: 10 am - 4 pm; Tuesday: Closed — Adults: €12

claim: The Acropolis Museum's second-floor cafe-restaurant and its terrace, which face the Acropolis directly, can be visited without buying a museum ticket.
quote: You can visit the cafe/restaurant of the Acropolis Museum without buying a museum ticket.

claim: Filopappou Hill is free and open 24/7, 15-20 minutes' walk from the Acropolis, gives the classic head-on Parthenon view, needs sensible shoes on its marble paths, and is best avoided after dark.
quote: Filopappou Hill is completely free to visit and "open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week so you can visit any time you wish." ... authorities recommend avoiding nighttime visits

claim: The Lycabettus funicular from Kolonaki costs EUR 10 return / EUR 7 one-way and runs every 30 minutes from 09:00 to 02:30; the walk up takes about 45 minutes.
quote: Round-trip: €10; One-way: €7 ... Runs every 30 minutes from 9:00 AM to 2:30 AM ... Approximately 45 minutes to summit via tree-lined path

claim: A single Athens morning fits either the Acropolis Museum or the National Archaeological Museum but not both; Benaki and Cycladic are strong 1-1.5 hour second-tier picks, while the Byzantine Museum, National Gallery and smaller specialist museums are afternoon filler.
quote: A single quality morning allows time for either the Acropolis Museum OR the National Archaeological Museum—not both.

claim: The Acropolis Restoration Service completed the Parthenon's west pediment and permanently removed the western scaffolding on 15 June 2026, the first time in about 220 years the west facade is whole.
quote: The restoration was completed on June 15, 2026, when 'the permanent removal of the scaffolding from the western side of the Parthenon' revealed the finished pediment.

claim: A timed ticket books your gate entry, not your place in the mandatory security screening, which can still take 15-30 minutes at peak; the once-quiet south-slope entrance now queues about as long as the west one.
quote: your timed slot refers to entry at the gate, not the security line ... while people often say the south entrance is much quicker, this advice usually comes from people who visited more than five years ago

claim: Exarchia is fine to walk by day but has gentrified fast, still hosts protests and riot-police deployments, and is the site of a contested Line 4 metro dig under Exarchia Square.
quote: During the day, Exarchia is fascinating and perfectly safe to explore ... the planned construction of a new metro station for Line 4 directly beneath Exarchia Square

claim: State sites are free on 6 March, 18 April, 18 May, the last September weekend and 28 October (plus winter Sundays); EU citizens under 25 are always free; on free days you still queue for a zero-cost ticket and should arrive before 08:00.
quote: visitors 'will still need to pick up a free ticket at the entrance' ... arriving 'before 8:00, as Greek people tend to visit much later'

claim: The August Full Moon night falls on Friday 28 August 2026, when 126 sites and museums open free from roughly 19:30-20:00 until 23:00-24:00, with extra events on 26-27 and 29-30 August.
quote: The primary celebration occurs on Friday, August 28, 2026 ... Most sites operate from 7:30-8:00 PM until 11:00 PM or midnight.

claim: The seven ex-combo sites now cost about EUR 105 bought separately; the Ancient Agora is the best-value add-on, the Roman Agora is justified by the Tower of the Winds, and the Olympieion doubled from EUR 8 to EUR 20 although all 15 columns are visible from the perimeter fence for free.
quote: The Temple of Olympian Zeus doubled in price from €8 to €20 in 2025, yet all 15 standing columns are "fully visible from the perimeter fence" without paying admission.

claim: Acropolis Museum highlights are the five original Caryatids and the Parthenon Gallery, rotated 23 degrees to align with the real Parthenon; allow 1.5-2.5 hours and visit the hill first, except on Friday evenings when the museum's late opening catches the sunset.
quote: rotated 23 degrees from the rest of the building to align exactly with the Parthenon ... an exception applies Friday evenings—start with the museum for optimal sunset lighting in the top gallery
